scope: One guarded 27B Q4 replacement-mode direct Reviewer request after stopping the idle owner 9B runtime; no installed profile or public release changed
reason: The prior concurrent 9B-plus-27B screen hit critical host pressure and could not establish whether the 27B model alone was feasible.

request.settings: Same source-bound Task06 direct-review prompt and sampler as the 9B thinking control; 4,096 max output tokens, 1,536 thinking budget, MTP disabled, no cache
request.temporary_server: Only model server on loopback port 8001, 19.5 GB oMLX memory guard, one concurrent request
request.external_guard: Abort on first host warning/critical sample or over 256 MiB swap growth, 0.5-second samples, 180-second timeout

quality: The model correctly identified JSON serialization as the failure source but proposed rows.join('\n') for an array of row objects. A disposable real-Chrome application of that exact proposal failed the first stored-markup probe: the inserted row ID never appeared within 10 seconds, so subsequent literal-text and inert-markup assertions were not reached. JavaScript joins row objects as [object Object]. No safe repair was produced.
owner_restore: The temporary 27B server exited; guarded kryn bench passed and doctor reported healthy Qwen3.5-9B-6bit at 65,536 context with the private 16 GiB guard, normal pressure and zero active requests. Host swap remained about 10.3 GiB allocated from the earlier concurrent failure; this short isolated screen added no sampled swap.
decision: The 27B model is feasible for one guarded 16K-context request as a replacement under this observed app load, unlike the failed concurrent configuration. Do not promote it: the source-bound repair failed, 64K long-workflow quality and sustained resource behavior are untested, and the existing 9B/64K profile remains the private rollback baseline.
limits: One prompt and one short request do not establish general quality, latency distribution, 64K support, warm/cold cache correctness, or active endurance. The real browser check was a same-account disposable proposal test, not protected evaluator qualification. No full autonomous coding/UI, semantic compaction/restart, second-account inference, or public release gate passed.
